examples.ko: 이번 주는 야근 강행군이라 너무 피곤해요.
examples.en: This week is a grind of overtime, so I'm exhausted.

examples.ko: 사흘 동안 강행군을 했더니 몸살이 났어요.
examples.en: After three days of nonstop pushing, I came down with aches.

examples.ko: 여행 일정이 강행군이어서 쉴 틈이 없었어요.
examples.en: The travel schedule was so packed that there was no time to rest.
After a punishing stretch of work, I finally finished the project.
During exam season, every day is a grind.

examples.ko: 강행군은 오래 하면 건강에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Pushing yourself nonstop for long is bad for your health.

explain: 일정이 빡빡해서 쉬지 못하고 계속 일하거나 움직이는 것을 말해요. 원래는 군대 행군에서 온 말이지만 일상에서는 여행, 일, 공부에 많이 써요. '강행군을 하다', '강행군이다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It describes working or moving nonstop on a packed schedule without rest. It comes from the idea of a forced military march, but in daily life it is used for trips, work and study. It is said as '강행군을 하다' or '강행군이다'.

examples.en: He made it big as a singer.
If you work hard, you will succeed big someday.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 재능이 있어서 대성할 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: He had talent from childhood, so I knew he'd go far.
To achieve great success, you need perseverance.
He is someone who left home and made it big in Seoul.

examples.ko: 대성하고 나서도 처음 마음을 잊지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even after becoming a great success, he did not forget his first resolve.

explain: 대성하다는 일이나 분야에서 크게 성공해 이름을 얻는다는 뜻이에요. 보통 미래에 대한 응원이나 덕담으로 '대성하세요', '대성할 거예요'라고 말해요. 그냥 '성공하다'보다 훨씬 크게 이루었다는 느낌이고, 주로 사람에게 쓰며 가수, 선수, 학자 같은 직업 이야기에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Daeseonghada means to succeed greatly and make a name for yourself in a field. It often appears in good wishes about the future, such as 대성하세요. It feels much bigger than plain 성공하다, and it is used for people, especially singers, athletes, and scholars.

examples.en: The evidence in this writing is too thin.
I ate a meager breakfast, so I'm hungry already.
That presentation was disappointing because the content was thin.
My health got worse because of a poor diet.
I was upset to hear that my imagination was poor.

examples.ko: 이야기 구성은 빈약했지만 그림은 정말 예뻤어요.
examples.en: The story structure was weak, but the pictures were really pretty.

explain: 근거, 내용, 상상력처럼 있어야 할 알맹이가 모자랄 때 써요. 반대는 '풍부하다'예요. 사람의 몸에 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있으니 조심하세요.
explain_en: Use it when the substance that should be there is lacking, as with evidence, content or imagination. The opposite is '풍부하다'. Be careful, since saying it about a person's body can be rude.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 선구적 기술로 시장을 이끌었어요.
examples.en: That company led the market with pioneering technology.
He is a scientist who played a trailblazing role.

examples.ko: 선구적 시도 덕분에 새로운 길이 열렸어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the pioneering attempt, a new path opened up.
For its time, this work was a pioneering experiment.
I met the professor who did the groundbreaking research.

examples.ko: 그 생각은 너무 선구적이어서 처음엔 이해받지 못했어요.
examples.en: That idea was so ahead of its time that it wasn't understood at first.

explain: 보통 '선구적 역할', '선구적 연구'처럼 명사 앞에 바로 써요. '선구적인', '선구적이다'로도 쓸 수 있어요. 처음으로 새 길을 연 일을 높이 평가하는 좋은 뜻의 말이에요.
explain_en: It usually goes straight before a noun, as in '선구적 역할' or '선구적 연구', and can also be used as '선구적인' or '선구적이다'. It carries a positive tone, praising someone for opening a new path first.

en: be on a fast track; go from strength to strength

examples.ko: 그 회사는 신제품 덕분에 승승장구하고 있어요.
examples.en: That company is going from strength to strength thanks to its new product.

examples.ko: 데뷔 후 계속 승승장구하던 배우가 쉬기로 했어요.
examples.en: The actor, who kept rising after his debut, decided to take a break.
I envy my friend who keeps succeeding.
You can't sail through successfully from the very start.
Our team is on a roll this season too.

examples.ko: 그는 입사 후 승승장구해서 빨리 팀장이 됐어요.
examples.en: He rose quickly after joining and became a team leader early.

explain: 일이 막힘없이 잘 풀려서 계속 앞으로 나아갈 때 써요. 주로 사람, 회사, 팀이 성공의 길을 달릴 때 말하고, 안 좋은 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used when things go smoothly and someone keeps advancing. It mostly describes a person, company or team on a streak of success, and is not used for bad things.

en: have a desperate fight; have a hard battle

examples.en: The new employees are struggling hard on the new project.
Rescue workers are fighting a hard battle in the heavy snow.
The team struggled hard with too few people.
Every exam period I feel like I'm battling my assignments.
The shop that had been struggling finally turned a profit.

examples.ko: 저는 오늘 아침 내내 컴퓨터 오류와 악전고투했어요.
examples.en: I battled a computer error all morning today.

explain: 눈앞의 어려움과 맞서 힘껏 버티며 싸울 때 써요. '~와/과 악전고투하다'처럼 맞서는 상대를 함께 말해요. 컴퓨터 오류와 싸운다고 말하듯 가벼운 일에 과장해서 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Use it when you struggle with all your might against a difficulty in front of you. You usually name the opponent, as in '~와/과 악전고투하다'. It is also used humorously for small things, like battling a computer error.

examples.en: I took an ethics class at university.

examples.ko: 동물 실험 문제로 윤리학 시간에 토론했어요.
examples.en: We debated the issue of animal testing in ethics class.
A professor who majored in ethics gave a lecture.

examples.ko: 윤리학 책이 어렵지만 생각할 거리가 많아요.
examples.en: Ethics books are difficult, but they give you a lot to think about.
Ethics also deals with what happiness is.
I read an article about AI and ethics.

explain: '윤리'는 지켜야 할 도덕적 기준 자체이고, '윤리학'은 그것을 연구하는 학문이에요. 철학의 한 분야로 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: '윤리' is the moral standard itself, while '윤리학' is the academic field that studies it. It often appears alongside philosophy as one of its branches.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 회의만 했더니 정신노동 때문에 지쳤어요.
examples.en: I did nothing but meetings all day, and the mental work wore me out.

examples.ko: 저는 정신노동보다 육체노동이 더 맞는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think physical work suits me better than mental work.

examples.ko: 번역은 몸은 편해도 정신노동이 많은 일이에요.
examples.en: Translation is easy on the body but involves a lot of mental work.

examples.ko: 정신노동도 오래 하면 몸이 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you do mental work for a long time, your body can hurt too.

examples.ko: 정신노동을 많이 한 날은 단 음식이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On days when I do a lot of mental work, I crave sweet food.
The line between physical and mental labor is getting blurrier.

explain: '육체노동'과 짝이 되는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '머리를 쓰는 일'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the counterpart of '육체노동' (physical labor). In everyday talk people often say '머리를 쓰는 일' (work that uses your head) instead.
